newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk leads Russian share index to record.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk leads Russian share index to record.

text.p: Leading Russian metals producer Norilsk Nickel fueled Russian shares to a third consecutive record close on Friday after traders saw signs the troubled company was sorting out its finances.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index powered to a record high finish of 390.82 on a record high total market turnover of $77.3 million. The index's close on Thursday, the previous record, was 388.99.
"Norilsk put out its pre-tax profit on Friday -- the market rose only on that," said United Financial Group trader Maxim Perlin.

Norilsk posted pre-tax profit to Russian accounting standards on a cash basis of 1.52 trillion roubles, down from 5.64 trillion roubles in 1995. It also posted a 3.29 trillion roubles consolidated loss reported.
Norilsk surged 17 percent to $8.56 as the market closed. The price was not an official closing price.
Renaissance Capital trader Timofey Demchenko said big investor interest in Norilsk had still not been satisfied but that the stock was not likely to rise much further.
"Orders are closer to the offer price," he said. "But prices are very high and I don't think there will be any further strong rise."
National power company UES rose to $0.3314 from $0.3270 despite parliament's announcement of plans to limit the share of nonresidents to 25 percent of the company's capital.
Natural gas monopoly Gazprom slipped to $0.555 from $0.571.

The powerful gas company announced on Friday it would issue a $1 billion Eurobond and a $1 billion convertible bond in 1997 or early 1998, as well as a second $1 billion Eurobond backed by gas exports.
Traders were divided on the market's direction next week.
"This long-awaited optimism is not going to go away that quickly," Demchenko said. "I think next week we are going to see the index setting more new records."
But the head of trading at Rinaco Plus, Alfred Kukk, said the market could go either way.

"It (the rise) could end soon, since it has been growing for a long time now, and the financial indicators are such that the limit of the growth is already close and for some companies, in my opinion, it has already arrived," he said.
But UFG's Perlin said the blue chip market was fairly strong and a rise on the second tier of less liquid shares could now start.
